To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed approach allows for the provision of route directions to wayfinders without prior knowledge, and the approach is generic, i.e. it is not bound to a particular modality.

1) a dialog-driven process of route direction generation is feasible, 2) it is feasible to generate route directions in a way that the wayfinder can control the level of detail of the route direction, 3) the wayfinder can adjust this level of detail during the navigation, 4) the wayfinder does not need any previous information about the route to be navigated, 5) the wayfinder only has to provide the information that he or she wants to receive.

(1) route directions are not static, and (2) the adaptation of route directions to the user’s knowledge is not based on the user’s previous knowledge, but on a dynamic dialog between a navigation system and the user.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: How can the type and amount of route directions provided to a wayfinder be adapted based on the assumed spatial knowledge?
the question of how a system should adapt the information it provides to a wayfinder in order to support him/her in the best way.
the question of how to support wayfinders in the process of generating a cognitive map of a new environment, and how to support them in finding their way in such environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper presents an approach for the generation of adaptive route directions based upon a dialog between a navigation system and its user.
the approach is a first step towards a more adaptive and personalized route direction service.
the approach provides the means to dynamically adapt route directions to the wayfinder’s spatial knowledge and the wayfinder’s needs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the paper provides a first approach towards a dynamic, dialog-driven process of route direction generation.
we provide a framework for the generation of personalized, dialog-driven route directions.
we are able to generate route directions for different levels of spatial knowledge of the wayfinder, and that this is achieved in a dialog-driven manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of turn by turn and destination descriptions provides an effective and efficient basis for adaptive route directions.
the combination of turn-byturn directions and descriptions can provide a more flexible way of route directions, which can be adapted to individual users.
the generation of adaptive route directions can be achieved by a combination of turn-based route directions with destination descriptions.
